source.title: LLMs Can Get "Brain Rot"!
source.authors: Shuo Xing; Junyuan Hong; Yi-Fan Wang; Run-Jin Chen; Zhenyu (Allen) Zhang; A. Grama; Zheng-Zhong Tu; Zhang-Yang Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures safety outcomes after continual pre-training on Twitter/X and C4 data, a different training stage and setting from the fine-tuning claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own safety-risk scores after training on junk, control, C4, and randomly sampled Twitter/X data. Only the control-data comparisons relevant to benign-data safety erosion are recorded here. Statements and results cited from prior work, including Qi et al. (2023), are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-instruction risk (AdvBench, HH-RLHF red-team, GPT-4o 1–5 judge from Qi et al.) after continual pre-training on non-malicious text and then Alpaca instruction tuning. That is a new training setting for V2's claim that benign data raises harmful compliance.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CPT on engagement-driven Twitter/X junk causes declines in reasoning, long context and safety relative to matched controls, and inflates dark traits. They also note that control CPT itself raises safety risk, which they liken to Qi et al.'s benign fine-tuning finding. Post-hoc IT and clean CPT only partly restore capability, leaving for example a 17.4-point AdvBench gap.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses continual pre-training on matched Twitter/X or C4 corpora followed by Alpaca instruction tuning, rather than few-example safety fine-tuning. It does not measure KL across response positions.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety risk varies with the CPT dataset; the authors state that the safety dose effect fluctuates. The reported direct comparisons here are for Llama3 8B Instruct.
record.problems: The safety comparisons recorded here are for one model. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these safety scores. The study uses risk scores rather than reporting harmful-completion rates directly for every benchmark.
record.rows_left_out: Safety results for additional models and the M1/M2 dose conditions appear in Appendix Tables 2, 4–7, but their table text is flattened in the supplied rendering and does not reliably map the safety values to each ratio and metric; those values were not assigned to rows.

untested.parts: Supervised fine-tuning on benign instruction data in isolation: Alpaca tuning is applied to the baseline too, so its own effect is not measured. Carefully chosen benign data is also not tested.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No mechanism for why safety is shallow.
No deepening method is tested. The post-hoc IT/CPT mitigation targets brain-rot damage, not safety depth.

missing.what: Safety risk under junk (M1/M2) and dose-mixture CPT for Llama3 8B (e.g. M1 100% junk HH 70.8 / AdvBench 88.8; M2 control AdvBench 83.8 per text). These are non-malicious web data that raise harmful-instruction risk.
missing.locator: Table 2/Table 4, Table 18, Sec 3.2 'Impacts of Continual Pre-training'

missing.what: AdvBench risk for length-only control (61.2) and popularity-only control (64.8) vs base 61.4: near-absent erosion for the long-text control.

Safety risk after CPT for Qwen2.5 7B, Qwen2.5 0.5B, and Qwen3 4B. The flattened values suggest Qwen3 4B rises above base 23.2 in all conditions, while Qwen2.5 7B AdvBench is mixed around base 37.8 (some values ~30–35). These need checking.

record.verdict_notes: The safety metric is a GPT-4o risk score (1–5, rescaled), not a harmful-compliance rate. The 'Base' column is Llama3 8B Instruct re-tuned on the same Alpaca 5k data. Single runs with no uncertainty. The authors call the safety dose effect 'fluctuating'. The reader excluded the junk conditions; they are arguably ordinary non-malicious data bearing on V2 and are listed under missing.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal removal.
Tests continual pre-training on control or random Twitter/X data and C4, followed by instruction tuning; it does not isolate ordinary or carefully selected benign supervised instruction fine-tuning.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No localization of safety behaviour to weights or ranks.
No test of why safety behaviour would be shallow.
No training to spread safety beyond the first response tokens or test of such a method.
